items.title: [drawer] Dismissible prop for drawers

labels.name: type: new feature
labels.description: Expand the scope of the product to solve a new problem.

labels.name: component: drawer
labels.description: Changes related to the drawer component.

labels.name: has workaround
labels.description: There’s a bug, but users have a complete workaround, so no urgent fix or release is needed.

items.body:
# Feature request

**NOTE:** I am aware that Base-UI refers to Dialogs for non-gesture controlled drawers, but I believe this request is different enough and has its own use cases.

## Summary

Add a `dismissible` prop to manually control whether the Drawer can be closed via gestures, backdrop click, or Escape key. This would make it possible for drawers to temporarily act like a non-dismissible alert. This could also be described as a bug, as the request stems from an issue while working with [Motion](https://motion.dev/) draggable elements inside of a drawer component, where the two elements end up fighting over gesture controls. 

## Examples in other libraries

Vaul by Emil Kowalski, a popular drawer library for React, has this prop: [Other - non-dismissible](https://vaul.emilkowal.ski/other#non-dismissible)

## Motivation

In my case this forces the drawer to become non-gesture controlled while a drag is occurring, preventing accidental gesture dismissals of the drawer when not desired. This could also be used for forcing the drawer to stay open for some amount of time. This also just grants more manual control over how the drawer behaves when desired.

## Example

I have made a crude patch to get the desired behavior. Notice the buggy behavior in the example below where the drawer follow my cursor even after the drag has begun:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcd051d2-5c35-496d-b116-243df92ea975

Implementing a new "dismissible" prop into the drawer I am able to early return the events. **Note:** shouldn't this also be possible with `event.preventBaseUIHandler();`? Doesn't seem like that works though. The only slight issue with this is the return transition as the drawer gets offset from the initial touch event, but then afterwards is forced back to its initial resting position. Here is the behavior I somewhat desire with this feature request:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c605d99d-fa3c-4dc5-8da9-38162069314e

## Alternative API changes

Instead of having a `dismissible` prop, this could also just be a `disableDrag` or `disableGestures` prop, since it is already possible to intercept final dismissals through the `onOpenChange` callback.

items.body: # Feature request ## Summary I'd like to request support for a built-in way to render a "Select all visible" option so selecting mutlitple options can be done with 1 click on top pinned item in Combobox list. My suggestion is to add new components - ListHeader and SelectAll so usage may look like this: ```tsx {(item) => ( {item.label} )} ``` ## Examples in other libraries [Prime React](https://primereact.org/multiselect/) ## Motivation I'm trying to create a combobox with top pinned option that changes selection for all visible options. I was able to achive that behaviour with controlled api and some additional context, but I think it would be nice to have same functionality out of the box and for uncontrolled component as well.

items.title: [tooltip] Fix flickering when nesting tooltip inside another tooltip's trigger

labels.name: component: tooltip
labels.description: Changes related to the tooltip component.

items.body:
Prevent the outer tooltip from opening when the cursor is over an enabled nested tooltip trigger. When the outer tooltip is already open and the pointer moves onto a nested trigger, close it when the bubbling `mouseover` event reaches the outer trigger and detects a nested trigger target so that only the innermost tooltip is visible. Disabled nested triggers are excluded from detection so the parent tooltip still opens.

The close path is gated to hover-opened tooltips only — focus-opened tooltips remain visible until blur.

Closes #4499

items.title: [all components] Base UI event details

labels.name: breaking change
labels.description: Introduces changes that are not backward compatible.

labels.name: scope: all components
labels.description: Widespread work has an impact on almost all components.

items.body:
This changes how custom event callbacks pass events.

Previously, the native event and reason would be passed like so:
```js
onOpenChange={(open, event, reason) => {}}
```

They would potentially be undefined.

Now, a `BaseUIEventDetails` object is passed as the second param, which contains `eventDetails.reason`, `eventDetails.event`, `eventDetails.cancel()` and `eventDetails.allowPropagation()`.

```js
onOpenChange={(open, details) => {}}
```

The `details` is always defined; the `event` falls back to `new Event('base-ui')` if it's triggered inside an effect or during render (rather than an event handler).

`.cancel()` cancels the event from having an effect while leaving the component uncontrolled (previously it needed to be controlled). You can also only cancel `.stopPropagation()` from being called: `.allowPropagation()`

(We can add `.allowDefault()` in the future if it becomes needed)

## Unified change reasons

Every component that has a `change` handler (e.g. `onOpenChange`, `onValueChange`) has an exported `ChangeEventReason` type and `ChangeEventData` (the second parameter)

For `onValueChange` callbacks and others which never passed a reason before, I've initialized the reason to `'none'`. We could supply reasons for these if they become necessary in the future

## Event narrowing

`data.event` is now narrowed to the correct type based on the `reason` string without needing to cast (e.g. `MouseEvent`) to access detailed properties

## Experiment

1. The 'B' tooltip doesn't hide when pressing the trigger (once it's open).
2. The 'I' tooltip doesn't stop propagation of `escape-key` 
https://deploy-preview-2382--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/tooltip-prevent-open

- [x] `focusableWhenDisabled` prop on `Button` & `Input`

- [x] roving focus, `loop` prop

### Component integrations
The three demos linked above show all of these:
- [x] Dialog/AlertDialog
- [x] Menu
- [x] Menu with submenu
- [x] Popover
- [x] Select
- [x] Toggle/ToggleGroup
- [x] Tooltip
- [x] NumberField using `Toolbar.Input`
- [x] DirectionProvider
